title: Legacy Business Insights help: architecture, data sources and terminology (hub)

prose.label: Where the details are.
prose.text: Portal administration, roles, admins, audit logs and the ZIA sync pages are in [[business-insights.legacy.admin]]. Admin password expiration, SCIM, SAML and sign-in are in [[business-insights.legacy.authentication]]. Workflow Automation SaaS application tenants are in [[business-insights.legacy.workflow]]. Application Insights, application details, custom signatures and application tags are in [[business-insights.legacy.applications]]. Contracts, the processing queue and contract tags are in [[business-insights.legacy.contracts]]. Workplace Insights, discovered locations and the map and chart views are in [[business-insights.legacy.workplace]]. Offices, goals, department mapping and workplace tags are in [[business-insights.legacy.offices]]. System, workplace, application and Data Explorer reports and the exclusion list are in [[business-insights.legacy.reports]].
Whether the legacy UI is still reachable is open {{gap:legacy-ui-status}}. The current product is described in [[business-insights.overview]].

prerequisites.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, SaaS app insights require a Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) subscription; workplace insights also require Zscaler Client Connector deployed on the relevant endpoints.

quotes: To gain SaaS app insights, you must be subscribed to the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service.
To gain workplace insights, in addition to the ZIA service, you must have Zscaler Client Connector deployed on all relevant endpoints you want to track for office utilization.

data-sources.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Business Insights receives signals from 4 data sources: ZIA, identity providers such as Okta and Entra ID, SaaS application connector integrations for Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google and GitHub, and custom application signatures.

quotes: Business Insights receives signals and data from 4 data sources: the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service that acts as one of the input feeders, identity providers (IdPs) like Okta and Entra ID, SaaS application connector integrations
(supported for apps such as Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google, and GitHub), and custom application signatures.

discovery-scale.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps, but by default the portal shows only a subset depending on business relevance.

quotes: Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps. By default, only a subset of these apps are shown in the portal, depending on your business relevance

usage-thresholds.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, High Usage Apps have over 80% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users, and Low Usage Apps have less than 30%.

quotes: High Usage Apps: Apps with over 80% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.
Low Usage Apps: Apps with less than 30% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.

engagement-index.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Without plan details, the Engagement Index is the percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days; with plan details it is active users in the last 30 days over purchased seats, falling back to assigned seats and then to the no-plan calculation, and showing the plan with the lowest index when several plans exist.

quotes: Without Plan Details: The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days for an app.
With Plan Details: The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the number of purchased seats for an app.
If the data of the purchased seats is unavailable, the service replaces it with the number of assigned seats.

If both the data are unavailable, the service defaults to the preceding calculation performed for apps without plan details. If multiple plans exist, the service shows the data for the plan with the lowest engagement index.

growth-trend.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Growth Trend is the percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days, calculated as the change in active users divided by the active users before the last 30 days, times 100.

quotes: Growth Trend: The percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days.
the growth trend is calculated by dividing the increase or decrease in the number of active users by the number of active users before the last 30 days, and multiplying it by 100

active-users-seats.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Active users have accessed or used the app at least once in the last 30 days; Purchased Seats is the seats bought within a subscription plan (one seat per user) and Assigned Seats is the seats assigned to users from them.

quotes: Active users have accessed or used the app at least once in the last 30 days.
Purchased Seats: The number of seats purchased within a subscription plan. One seat is assigned to one user.
Assigned Seats: The number of seats assigned to users from the purchased seats.

workplace-types.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Workplaces are of two types, Inferred Locations (individual ZIA locations and inferred IP addresses) and Configured Offices (groupings of inferred locations with metadata).

quotes: There are two types of workplaces:
Inferred Locations: These are individual ZIA locations configured in the ZIA Admin Portal
Configured Offices: These are the grouping of inferred locations into a configured office with metadata.
and inferred IP addresses that the Business Insights service concludes as the organization's workplace

attendance-occupancy-terms.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Average Attendance is total visits divided by total assigned headcount, times 100, and Average Occupancy is total visits divided by site capacity, times 100; Assigned Headcount is the users assigned to an office and Capacity is the employees it can accommodate.

quotes: The average attendance for an office site is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplace by the total number of assigned headcount for the workplace, then multiplying it by 100.
The average occupancy for a workplace is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplace by the site capacity, then multiplying it by 100.
Assigned Headcount: The number of users assigned to an office.
Capacity: The number of employees the office can accommodate.

inferred-location-basis.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Business Insights concludes inferred IP addresses are a workplace based on the amount of traffic, the number of users behind the IP address, and more assuring metrics.

quotes: inferred IP addresses that the Business Insights service concludes as the organization's workplace based on the amount of traffic, the number of users behind the IP address, and more assuring metrics.

legacy-ui-status.title: Whether the legacy Business Insights UI is still reachable and which release replaced it
legacy-ui-status.detail: The legacy articles describe the Business Insights Admin Portal with its own Administration, Applications and Workplaces menus. They do not say whether that UI is still reachable or which release replaced it with the current Internet & SaaS and Analytics > Business Insights pages.
